common_name: Kagami Jishi Leopard Plant (Crested Leopard Plant)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; 'Kagami Jishi' combines the yellow spotting of 'Aureomaculatum' with the ruffled leaf margins of 'Crispatum', so give it a sheltered site where its distinctive foliage can be seen up close.

directions: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, sheltered from harsh afternoon sun that scorches the crimped leaf edges. 'Kagami Jishi' is a smaller-scale leopard plant selection prized for rounded, glossy green leaves that are both irregularly spotted in gold and tightly ruffled along the margins, pairing two ornamental traits found separately in other farfugium cultivars. Tall stalks of yellow daisy-like flowers rise above the clump in mid to late fall, extending garden interest well past the point when most shade perennials have finished blooming. Its compact habit and eye-catching texture make it well suited to a shaded container, entry planting, or the front of a woodland border where finer detail can be appreciated.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

common_name: Green Teeth Leopard Plant (Formosan Leopard Plant)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in moist, well-drained soil in part sun to light or full shade; unlike typical broad-leaved farfugium, 'Green Teeth' comes from open grassland habitat in Taiwan and tolerates more sun than most leopard plant selections.

directions: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in moist, well-drained soil in part sun to light or full shade, giving it room to spread since it forms a wide, low clump. 'Green Teeth' is a wild-collected Taiwanese selection of the formosanum variety with a strikingly different look from typical leopard plant, bearing smaller, thicker, sharply pointed-lobed leaves rather than the broad rounded foliage of the species. Bright yellow daisy-like flowers rise on stalks to about two feet starting in mid-October, extending well past the bloom time of most other shade perennials. Because it naturally grows in open grassland rather than deep woodland, it accepts more light than other farfugium and makes a good textural contrast planted among broader-leaved shade companions.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden
